interface.title: Research Hub
interface.field: Biomedical and general scholarly literature search (bibliometrics / evidence synthesis)
interface.stage_of_work: Literature discovery and scoping at the start of a literature review
interface.what_it_is_for: Turn a plain-language research focus into per-database Boolean queries, search PubMed, Europe PMC and OpenAlex together, and save and export the results as a named research note and a Word document.

data.note: No data is bundled and nothing is uploaded. Every result came live from the public PubMed, Europe PMC and OpenAlex APIs, using typed focuses: the README examples 'dopamine reward learning in rodent models of addiction' and 'lipid nanoparticle mRNA delivery cancer', a full-sentence CRISPR / sickle-cell question, and a keyword version of it. One PubMed call failed once with HTTP 502 and worked when re-run.

features.name: Plain-language-to-Boolean query builder with per-source transparency panel
features.general: Turn a free-text topic into search strings formatted for each target database, show each string under its database name, and let the user copy it to check or reuse
features.specific: Research focus text → key-term extraction (up to 7 terms for PubMed, 6 for Europe PMC and OpenAlex; filler words are not removed) → the first 4 terms are joined with AND and any remaining terms are OR'd as one group: PubMed [Title/Abstract] query, Europe PMC TITLE:/ABSTRACT: query, OpenAlex keyword string → 'Queries sent to each source' expander with sideways-scrolling, copyable code blocks
steps: Type a topic or a full sentence into Research focus
Run the search
Expand 'Queries sent to each source'
Read or sideways-scroll each database's query
Press Copy to clipboard to reuse the query in the database's own site, or reword the focus and run again
serves_tasks: Check the exact search strings sent to each database
Describe the topic in plain language and name the record
Reword the topic after reading the generated search strings and search again

features.name: Multi-database source selector with per-source result cap
features.general: Choose one, several or all bibliographic databases to search, and cap how many records come back from each
features.specific: Data source dropdown (All sources / PubMed / Europe PMC / OpenAlex / Europe PMC + OpenAlex) with help tooltip, plus Max papers slider 1–20 applied per source. The Papers found / Sources metrics and the 'Sources queried' line show the result
steps: Open the Data source dropdown and pick a source set
Drag or arrow-key the Max papers slider
Run research (button or Ctrl+Enter)
Read Papers found and Sources, which equal the cap times the number of sources when every source returns enough hits
serves_tasks: Limit how many results each database returns
Narrow the search to one database or a subset
Search all databases at once and get one combined list

features.name: Source-tagged consolidated paper list
features.general: Show results from several databases in one scrolling list of cards, each tagged with the database it came from and linking to the original record
features.specific: Top papers: cards with a coloured pubmed / europe_pmc / openalex badge, title, 'journal | year | authors', a truncated abstract ('No Abstract available' when missing) and an 'Open paper' link. A 'Primary reference' link is shown above the list. Cards are grouped by source and not de-duplicated
steps: Run a search
Read the Papers found / Sources summary and the Primary reference link
Scroll the Top papers cards, using the source badge to tell origins apart
Follow 'Open paper' to the PubMed / Europe PMC / OpenAlex record
serves_tasks: Search all databases at once and get one combined list
Narrow the search to one database or a subset

features.name: Named search record (auto-save + raw JSON copy)
features.general: Save each search under a user-chosen name as a structured record (inputs, queries, timestamp, results) that can be inspected and copied right after the search
features.specific: Note name + Run research → 'Saved note: …' banner and a notebook.db entry. The 'Raw output JSON' expander shows status, note_saved_as, timestamp, sources_queried, queries_used, papers[] and details.source_breakdown[], and has a copy button. Re-using a note name saves again with no warning
steps: Enter a Note name and run the search
Confirm the 'Saved note: <name>' banner
Expand 'Raw output JSON'
Press the copy icon to take the JSON record
serves_tasks: Save a named record of the search (query, sources, results)

features.name: Per-source status and error report
features.general: Report, for each database searched, how many records it returned, the exact query used and any error, so an empty or short result can be traced to its cause
features.specific: details.source_breakdown[] inside the 'Raw output JSON' expander, one entry per source with results, reference, query_used and error (e.g. 'Pubmed 2.0 search API: HTTP request returned 502 status'). The page itself shows only 'No relevant papers found' and status still reads 'Success'
steps: Run a search and notice 0 papers or fewer than expected
Expand 'Raw output JSON'
Scroll to details.source_breakdown and read each source's results and error
If the error is transient (e.g. HTTP 502), run the search again
serves_tasks: Diagnose why a search returned nothing

features.name: Word export of search results
features.general: Download the current result set as an editable document named after the record, ready to drop into a review
features.specific: 'Export as Word (.docx)' downloads <Note_name>.docx (spaces become underscores) for the current results, then the page reruns and clears the results panel. Per the app code (_build_word_export), the document holds the note name, focus, source, limit, timestamp, the query for each database, a summary, and for each paper its source, journal, year, authors, link and abstract (not checked inside the downloaded files)
steps: Run a search so results are showing
Press 'Export as Word (.docx)'
Collect <Note_name>.docx from downloads
serves_tasks: Export the results as a document for the literature review

screens_never_reached: A list or browser of saved notes: notes are written to notebook.db, but the UI has no view to list, reopen, rename or delete them. Reloading the page brings back an empty form (screens/047.webp)

The rendered contents of the exported .docx: the files downloaded (38–43 KB), but the reader reports them only as binary. What they contain is known only from the app code (_build_word_export), not from opening a file

A result's full record in its source database (Open paper / Primary reference): the links point to pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, europepmc.org and openalex.org, which were off-limits for this session, so this step was skipped on purpose
not_done: Opening the Word exports: the .docx files are binary to the download reader. Their contents are stated from the app code only, not checked in the files
Reopening a saved note: the UI has no control for it. The record can only be seen as Raw output JSON straight after a search
Telling whether re-using a note name overwrites or duplicates the earlier note: the app saved 'Dopamine addiction review' a second time with no warning and offers no notes view
Following 'Open paper' / Primary reference links: they lead to pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, europepmc.org and openalex.org, which are off-limits for this session

Observed limitations, not things left undone: (1) pressing Export reruns the page and clears the results panel (screens/018.webp, screens/054.webp); (2) results from different databases are not de-duplicated, so the same paper appears under pubmed and europe_pmc; (3) key-term extraction keeps at most 7 (PubMed) / 6 (Europe PMC, OpenAlex) terms and keeps filler words, so 'How effective is CRISPR base editing for correcting sickle cell disease…' became 'effective crispr base editing correcting sickle' and returned an off-topic heart-failure paper first (screens/034.webp); (4) when a source fails, the page shows only 'No relevant papers found' and the JSON status still reads 'Success'. The real error is only in the raw JSON; (5) the main-menu Light/Dark theme has no visible effect because the app's own styling overrides it (screens/045.webp); (6) in the replay, Europe PMC cards showed 'Unknown Journal' and raw <h4>/<b> tags in abstracts
